title: Two places in one pool
question: In pre-qualified pools and as-needed lists, are two or more members one owner-group, and what share of the work did they take together?
finding: 50 as-needed or pool contract titles have 3 or more different prime contractors. In 3 of them two members are tied: 0 set(s) on record evidence (tiers 1 to 4), 0 on a shared address only, and 3 where a firm holds its own place and is also a member of a joint venture in the same pool.
how: A pool is one department’s contract title that contains "as-needed", "pool", "on-call", "pre-qualified", "job order" or "master agreement" and has at least 3 different prime contractors in the Controller’s contract file. Every pair of primes is tested against the owner-groups and address leads, and against the file’s own list of joint-venture members. The share is the tied members’ payments over all payments under that title; agreed amounts are shown beside them.
limits: Pools are found from contract titles, so differently titled rounds of one pool are separate rows and pools with other wording are missed. Whether a firm may hold a place alone and also through a joint venture in the same pool is set by the solicitation, which is not in these files and should be checked. Subcontractors are ignored: a pool member working as another member’s subcontractor is common and is not counted. Payments recorded as zero mean the file shows none, not that no work was done.
